audit_metadata.project: SIH Problem Statement 26074 (Weather Downscaling from Block to Panchayat Level)
audit_metadata.purpose: Reconciliation of Condition History CRPS vs Bootstrap Case-Level CRPS Point Estimates
audit_metadata.canonical_aggregation_definition: Case-Preserving Weighted Sample Mean: M = (1 / N_total) * sum_{i=1}^{N_total} M_i

root_cause_analysis.mathematical_mechanism: evaluate_sprint8_ensemble.py accumulated batch-averaged CRPS into all_crps_list (length 31) and computed np.mean(all_crps_list). This assigned the final batch of 2 cubes an unweighted 1/31 (3.2258%) weight instead of its legitimate 2/122 (1.6393%) sample weight. Because the 31st batch contained late-monsoon heavy-rain events with high error (CRPS ~ 3.8070 vs ~0.4961 across batches 1-30), giving it double weight pushed the unweighted batch mean upward by ~0.0525 points across all conditions. The bootstrap pipeline correctly computed the metric per case, assigning each cube uniform weight 1/122 (0.8197%).
root_cause_analysis.ranking_impact: ZERO. The relative ranking across all configurations is 100% preserved and strictly monotonic between both aggregations. K=2, S=16 remains the top continuous distribution performer, while K=8, S=4, eta=0.5 remains the top point-forecast and storm-recall performer.

invariants_adopted_for_sprint_8_5.canonical_crps_aggregation: np.average(case_crps, weights=None) where case_crps has length N_cases
invariants_adopted_for_sprint_8_5.batch_loop_rule: Accumulators must track (sum_of_case_metrics, total_cases_seen) rather than unweighted list of batch means
invariants_adopted_for_sprint_8_5.bootstrap_equivalence: Point estimate of bootstrap distribution is identically equal to the full dataset canonical sample mean
